title: U.S. Senate · New Hampshire

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Sen. Jeanne Shaheen (D) is retiring and did not run in the September 8, 2026 Democratic primary. U.S. Rep. Chris Pappas won that primary with 64.6% of the vote over Karishma Manzur and others. John Sununu (a businessman and former faculty member, not to be confused with his father, former Gov. John H. Sununu, or his brother, Gov. Chris Sununu) won the Republican primary with 68.4% over Scott Brown. Sununu previously served one term in the U.S. Senate (2003-2009) after defeating Shaheen in 2002; Shaheen defeated him in a 2008 rematch. He announced his candidacy on October 22, 2025 after Shaheen announced her retirement.

candidates.name: Chris Pappas
candidates.ballotNote: Won the September 8, 2026 Democratic primary with 64.6% of the vote.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for New Hampshire's 1st District (since 2019)

summary.text: Chris Pappas is the Democratic nominee for the open New Hampshire U.S. Senate seat. He is the sitting U.S. Representative for New Hampshire's 1st District, a former state legislator and Executive Council member, and co-owner of his family's restaurant.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in government from Harvard in 2002.

Elected to two terms in the New Hampshire House of Representatives, serving from 2003 to 2007, then served as treasurer of Hillsborough County from 2007 to 2011 and as a New Hampshire Executive Council member from 2013 to 2019.
Was the first openly gay U.S. House member elected from New Hampshire.
Is a co-owner of his family's restaurant.

priorities.text: Says he is focused on affordability and the economy, working to lower costs for families and small businesses on utilities, groceries, child care, health care and housing.
His campaign says he called for a ban on stock trading by members of Congress and forced a floor vote on the issue, and worked to cap the cost of insulin at $35.

positions.summary: On the New Hampshire Executive Council, voted to expand Medicaid to bring down health care costs and increase access for tens of thousands of Granite Staters.

record.text: Sits on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs and the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: Pappas has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; positions drawn from his campaign website as quoted by Ballotpedia. His federal key votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script.

candidates.name: John Sununu
candidates.ballotNote: Won the September 8, 2026 Republican primary with 68.4% of the vote over Scott Brown.
candidates.currentRole: Former U.S. Senator (2003-2009); faculty member, St. Anselm College

summary.text: John Sununu is the Republican nominee for the open New Hampshire U.S. Senate seat. He previously served one term as a U.S. Senator from 2003 to 2009 after unseating Jeanne Shaheen in 2002; Shaheen defeated him in a 2008 rematch. He announced this campaign after Shaheen's retirement.

background.text: Born in Salem, New Hampshire; worked in engineering, consulting and manufacturing, including running operations at an electronics company.
Served in the U.S. House of Representatives from 1997 to 2003, then in the U.S. Senate from 2003 to 2009.
As of 2026, served as a faculty member at St. Anselm College and as a director at Boston Scientific.
Is the son of former Gov. John H. Sununu (R) and the brother of Gov. Chris Sununu (R).

priorities.text: In an interview with The Dartmouth, said New Hampshire needs "an effective voice in Washington" focused on "the economy, jobs, affordability, housing, energy and healthcare," and described Congress as dysfunctional.
priorities.quote: Politics isn't just about holding an office. It's about being an effective voice for the people you represent. Right now, New Hampshire needs someone who understands the state and who is focused on the right things: the economy, jobs, affordability, housing, energy and healthcare.

record.text: As a U.S. Senator (2003-2009), served on Senate committees during the 108th-110th Congresses; specific committee assignments and roll-call votes from that earlier tenure were not reviewed for this entry.

candidates.researchNotes: Sununu has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; priorities drawn from a media interview quoted by Ballotpedia.

summary.text: Edmond Laplante is the Constitution Party nominee for the open New Hampshire U.S. Senate seat. He is a Marine Corps veteran, longtime automotive mechanic, and New Hampshire state chairman of the Constitution Party.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 1999 to 2007.
Graduated from the Ohio Diesel and Gas Technical Institute in 1988 and has worked as an automotive mechanic for more than 40 years.
Is New Hampshire state chairman of the Constitution Party and a member of the SAU93 (Richmond) school board.

priorities.text: In his Candidate Connection survey, lists his three key campaign messages as constitutional compliance and limited government, protecting people's liberty, rights and financial well-being, and transparency and accountability.
